newsitem.title: USA: Merrill recommends overweight on Bulgaria Bradys.
newsitem.headline: Merrill recommends overweight on Bulgaria Bradys.

text.p: Merrill Lynch & Co Inc said it changed its recommendation on Bulgarian Brady bonds to overweight from underweight on expectations that the country will reach an agreement with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) by May.

"There is now a clear timetable for Bulgaria to reach an agreement with the IMF. We think an IMF agreement will be in place by May," said Joyce Chang, emerging markets debt strategist at Merrill Lynch in New York.
Chang told Reuters that Merrill's decision to overweight Bulgarian Bradys is also based on expectations that the Union of Democratic Forces (UDF) will win the general elections in April.
"I think it is very likely that the UDF will win the elections in April and they are more sympathetic to market-oriented reforms," Chang said.
She noted that the conservative spread compression on Bulgarian Brady instruments also leaves room for extremely attractive returns.

"If you look at a relatively conservative spread compression of 150 to 200 basis points, you would still leave (yield spreads of) Bulgaria (Bradys) significantly wider than Ecuador," Chang said, pointing out that investors would be posting returns for the year of 25 percent from the current levels for the uncollateralized bonds and 20 percent for the discount bonds.
